title: Customer handshake proofing and approval SLO - rough
body:
Purpose:

This is a working PRD sketch for two related capabilities we keep being asked for in Private: (1) a tamper-evident customer handshake / evidence export for network handovers, and (2) firm SLOs and operational behavior for approval gates (latency, backpressure, and fallbacks).

High-level problem:
- Customers with strict audits need a compact, signed artifact that proves who approved a VPC/operator change, what the exact diff was, and evidence that the change was observed in the customer-managed network.
- Platform teams need predictable latency guarantees for approval workflows (so downstream services don't deadlock), and a clear fallback policy when customer-side connectivity or approvals are delayed.

Goals: (MVP scope)
- API to produce a single "handshake bundle" per approved network change. Bundle properties: human-readable summary, compact binary attachment of diffs, time-stamped approver signatures (operator + customer admin), and an immutable digest (SHA256) with platform-signed envelope.
- Export formats: JSON manifest + optional gzipped diff + base64 signatures. One-click export from Console and programmatic export API for S3 push or webhook.
- Define approval gate SLOs: P50/P90/P99 approval latency targets for CI/CD-like flows, and a policy for automatic timeout -> fallback model routing.
- Forensic replay: simple CLI tool (or script) to validate a bundle: verify signatures, verify digest, and optionally replay diff against a simulated network model for QA.

Non-goals (for MVP):
- Full cryptographic HSM integration for customer-supplied keys (we'll support later via KMS integration).
- Complex legal attestation packages.

User journeys (sketch):
1) Ad-hoc change (customer portal): Network admin submits edge-change bundle -> Request created -> internal operator reviews -> customer admin approves -> Platform generates handshake bundle -> stored in customer export bucket and marked as retained per retention policy.
2) Automated patch (operator-initiated with delegated approval): Operator triggers a change via API -> if delegated approval enabled, the system auto-signs with operator key and creates expected customer ack window -> if no ack, follow the fallback policy (see SLO section).

Handshake bundle contents (proposed manifest fields):
- bundle_id: opaque UUID
- created_at: ISO8601
- change_summary: short text
- change_diff_sha256: hex
- change_diff_uri: s3:// or internal artifact id (optional if included inline)
- approvers: list of {name, email, role, signed_key_id, signature_b64}
- platform_envelope_signature_b64: signature by Redwood signing key
- evidence_clips: [tcpdump-snippet-uri | config-snapshot-uri] (optional)
- retention_policy_label: e.g., 90d / 7y-compliant

Implementation notes (MVP technique):
- Signatures: use JOSE (compact JWS) with platform keypair. For operator signatures we use platform-managed keys tied to user identity (OIDC subject) — later we can add customer-supplied key fingerprints.
- Storage: bundle stored in per-customer exports bucket, access controlled by customer's RBAC and export ACL. Console shows most recent 30 bundles; full archive downloadable.
- Versioning: bundle manifests include schema_version. We keep v0, v1 etc to allow future cryptographic changes.

Approval SLOs and fallback behavior (proposal):
- SLO targets for interactive approval flows (measured from 'request created' to 'final approver signature accepted'):
  - P50: < 30s
  - P90: < 120s
  - P99: < 600s
- For machine-initiated flows where customer must ACK on their side (customer-managed network agent verification) we use longer SLO window but bounded: P90 < 15m, P99 < 2h.
- Backpressure and fallbacks:
  - If approval window exceeds configured timeout (customer-configurable at request template level; default 30m), the system marks the request as "timed_out" and triggers configured fallback: either (a) automatic rollback, (b) route traffic to a lower-privilege model variant (e.g., hosted fallback), or (c) pause and notify SRE/CS.
  - For Private deployments, default fallback should never route data outside customer scope without explicit consent. So default is (a) or (c) unless customer opted-in for (b).

Operational metrics we need to surface: (console + alerts)
- approval_latency histogram (per template, per customer)
- counts of timed_out approvals and chosen fallback paths
- bundle_generation_errors (parsing/signing/storage)
- export_delivery_failures (S3/webhook errors)

Retention and e-discovery:
- Support labels: short (90d), medium (2y), long (7y). Default label is short for non-enterprise customers.
- Allow customers to request bulk export for e-discovery with an authenticated job API (async) that returns a pre-signed archive link.

Security considerations:
- Bundle manifests may contain PII (approver emails). Default is redact emails in the Console UI; full manifest available only to customers and authorized Red team members with audit justification.
- Protect signing keys: keep platform signing keys in KMS; rotate quarterly. Record key version in manifest.
- Tamper evidence: on any bundle retrieval add Integrity header checksums to HTTP response; console will surface any mismatch.

Developer API sketch (examples):
- Create request: POST /api/v1/private/changes (body: change spec) -> returns request_id
- Approve: POST /api/v1/private/requests/{id}/approve (user token) -> returns signed fragment
- Export bundle: GET /api/v1/private/requests/{id}/bundle?format=inline|presigned -> returns manifest or presigned S3 link

CLI validation example (rough):
- redwood-private validate-bundle --file bundle.json
  - checks: signatures, digest equality, schema version supported

Rollout plan (phase-based):
- Phase 0 (experimental): internal-only bundles for a small set of enterprise customers; manual review on first 5 exports per customer.
- Phase 1 (MVP): Console export + API; retention labels; default SLOs and fallback policy configuration via tenant settings.
- Phase 2: Customer-supplied key support (KMS/HSM), deeper forensics (pcap replay), and legal attestation templates.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we need per-bundle notarization by an external CA for select customers? (security/legal asks for ledger-like proof)
- How granular should the default retention policy be? Can we let customers override at template-level or request-level only?
- UX: should Console show a minimal "proof card" vs. a full manifest download? (card preferred for most users)
- How do we reconcile bundles if customer-side agent has intermittent connectivity and partial evidence clips? Define partial-accept semantics.

Notes to self / engineering constraints:
- Keep initial manifest small (under 16KB) when diffs are externalized to avoid DB size pressure.
- Use existing signing infra used by rollout artifacts to reduce new surface area.

Next steps (short term):
- Sync with Security (Diego) about key rotation policy and minimum cryptographic primitives (deadline: 2/7).
- Draft an API spec (OpenAPI) and a minimal wire-format for the manifest (owner: Rohit, due 2/21).
- Create an internal spike for CLI validator and demo bundle generation (owner: Claire, due 3/1).

Related tickets and references:
- JIRA-PRIV-2101: customer export & retention
- CON-8342: detailed notes and mockups
- slack: #private-deploy-prod thread "handshake-export" (search-able)

-- end of draft --

(rough / notes style, expecting follow-ups; objective is to give eng & security a compact artifact to iterate from)
